items.headline: Ex-Singapore Idol judge Ken Lim appeals his molestation conviction and jail term
items.summary: Ken Lim, the former Singapore Idol judge, appealed in the High Court on Sep 11 against his conviction and 13-month sentence for molesting a woman at his Hype Records studio in 2021. His counsel argued the accuser’s account held contradictions; the judge reserved judgment.

items.headline: Lorry driver jailed 23 months over a red-light crash that disabled a cabby
items.summary: A 51-year-old lorry driver was jailed for 23 months and banned from driving for eight years after running a red light on Nicoll Highway in 2023 and hitting a taxi, Mothership reported. The 56-year-old cabby was left permanently disabled and later died; the driver pleaded guilty.

items.headline: Late lawyer’s son, acting pro bono, helps cut a first-time offender’s jail term
items.summary: A woman who cheated restaurants of about S$10,000 had her jail term reduced after the son of a late senior criminal lawyer took on her appeal without charge, Mothership reported, continuing the family’s record of free legal aid.

items.headline: India coverage is unavailable in today’s edition
items.summary: Every allowed India outlet — The Hindu, The Indian Express, Hindustan Times, The Times of India, NDTV and The Economic Times — along with the international fallback desks was unreachable from today’s run environment, so no India item could be verified to an allowed source. Coverage resumes tomorrow.

items.headline: PM Burnham pressed to define an economic plan as the Budget nears
items.summary: With a national Budget approaching, Prime Minister Andy Burnham faces pressure from within Labour to set out a defining economic strategy, Bloomberg reported, having promised a 10-year plan for Britain before year-end. Colleagues warn optimism alone will not ease the fiscal squeeze.

items.headline: RNLI lifeboat volunteers accused of ‘treason’ over Channel migrant rescues
items.summary: Volunteers at the charity-funded RNLI faced abuse and accusations of ‘treason’ for helping migrants ashore, CNN reported. In Portsmouth, activists led by Daniel Thomas tried to block lifeboats and buses heading to a processing centre.

items.headline: Britain enters winter with gas prices at multi-year highs and thin reserves
items.summary: UK wholesale gas prices have climbed to their highest since 2022, more than doubling since January, Bloomberg reported, while storage remains thin. Households face the steepest winter energy costs in three years.

items.headline: UK house prices stay under pressure as mortgage costs climb, surveyors say
items.summary: The RICS house-price balance was minus 28 in August, little changed from July and negative since April 2025, Bloomberg reported. Agents expect further falls over three months, with London weakest, amid pre-Budget tax-rise worries.

items.headline: CIA releases its largest tranche of pre-9/11 bin Laden briefings
items.summary: Marking the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, the CIA declassified dozens of presidential daily briefs on Osama bin Laden and al-Qaeda from before 2001, Al Jazeera reported — described as the agency’s largest release of such summaries.

items.headline: Canada matches US tariffs ‘dollar for dollar’ as the trade war deepens
items.summary: Canada began matching US tariffs after Washington imposed a 50% levy on about US$20 billion of Canadian goods, Al Jazeera reported. Prime Minister Mark Carney rebuffed US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick as households braced for the fallout.

items.headline: Serbia’s Vucic dissolves parliament and calls a snap election for Oct 25
items.summary: President Aleksandar Vucic dissolved parliament and set a snap parliamentary vote for October 25, Al Jazeera reported, after nearly two years of student-led anti-corruption protests sparked by the 2024 Novi Sad canopy collapse that killed 16.

items.headline: Rubio tours Latin America after a rightward shift across the region
items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio toured Ecuador, Peru and Colombia following right-wing electoral wins, Al Jazeera reported. Ecuador’s President Daniel Noboa awarded him a national honour, and Rubio held talks with Peru’s leadership in Lima.

items.headline: Tech & AI coverage is unavailable in today’s edition
items.summary: Today’s run could not reach or resolve a verifiable, non-duplicate article from the allowed technology outlets — The Verge, TechCrunch, Ars Technica, Wired, MIT Technology Review, The Information and the Reuters tech desk — which were blocked from the run environment. Coverage resumes tomorrow.

items.headline: Dell hits a record high after RBC starts coverage at Outperform
items.summary: Dell shares jumped about 11% to an all-time high on Friday after RBC Capital Markets began coverage with an Outperform rating and a $640 price target, CNBC reported, citing the company’s AI-server order backlog.

items.headline: AstraZeneca’s breast-cancer pill misses its goal in a late-stage trial
items.summary: AstraZeneca said its oral drug camizestrant, combined with Pfizer’s Ibrance, failed to meet the main progression-free-survival goal in the late-stage SERENA-4 trial, Bloomberg reported. US-listed shares slipped after hours.

items.headline: Novartis investor Artisan urges a board overhaul after two drug failures
items.summary: Artisan Partners’ David Samra, a top-20 Novartis shareholder, told Reuters the board needs a shake-up and tighter deal oversight after the failure of del-desiran — centrepiece of the $12 billion Avidity acquisition — and of the drug pelacarsen.

items.headline: Copper climbs to record highs on tariff fears and tight supply
items.summary: Copper has risen to record levels on the London Metal Exchange, Bloomberg reported, driven by expectations that US tariffs will extend to refined metal and by tight global supply as inventories are drawn toward US warehouses.

items.headline: 🎾 Shelton beats Tiafoe to reach his first US Open final
items.summary: Ben Shelton beat fellow American Frances Tiafoe 4-6, 6-3, 6-3, 7-5 to reach his first Grand Slam final — the first Black American man in a US Open singles final since Arthur Ashe, ESPN noted. He meets Alexander Zverev for the title.

items.headline: 🎾 Siniakova and Townsend complete a career Grand Slam in US Open doubles
items.summary: Top seeds Katerina Siniakova and Taylor Townsend rallied past Ashlyn Krueger and Robin Montgomery 5-7, 6-0, 6-2 to win the US Open women’s doubles title, completing the set of all four majors as a pairing.

items.headline: 🎾 Harrison and Skupski win the US Open men’s doubles title
items.summary: Christian Harrison of the US and Britain’s Neal Skupski beat Kevin Krawietz and Tim Puetz 6-4, 7-6(6) to take the US Open men’s doubles crown, adding to the Australian Open title they won together in January.

items.headline: 🏎️ Norris denies Antonelli pole for the Madrid Spanish Grand Prix
items.summary: Lando Norris took pole for the first Spanish Grand Prix at Madrid’s new Madring circuit, pipping Kimi Antonelli by 0.011 seconds, with Max Verstappen third. The 57-lap race runs Sunday.

items.headline: 🏎️ Sainz handed a three-place grid penalty for the Madrid race
items.summary: Carlos Sainz was given a three-place grid drop after stewards ruled he impeded Valtteri Bottas late in Madrid qualifying, Formula1.com reported. The Williams driver had qualified 17th for Sunday’s race.

items.headline: A newly found fast-moving star could reveal the Milky Way black hole’s spin
items.summary: Astronomers reported S301, a faint star on an 8.7-year orbit around Sagittarius A* reaching speeds near 25,000 km/s, Nature reported. Its tightly curved, relativistic orbit offers a direct way to measure how fast the galaxy’s central black hole spins.

items.headline: Menopause reshapes the brain in ways unlike pregnancy or puberty
items.summary: A new study finds distinct structural brain changes during menopause that differ from the remodelling seen in pregnancy and puberty, Scientific American reported, pointing to a unique neurological transition.

fun_fact.headline: An octopus has three hearts and blue blood
fun_fact.body: An octopus has three hearts: two pump blood through the gills, while a third drives it around the rest of the body. Its blood is blue because it carries oxygen using a copper-based molecule, hemocyanin, rather than the iron in ours. Stranger still, the main heart stops beating whenever the animal swims — part of why many octopuses prefer to crawl.

puzzle.title: The Seventh Floor
puzzle.body:
A man lives on the tenth floor of an apartment block. Every morning he takes the lift all the way down to the ground floor and heads to work. Each evening he rides the lift back up — but only to the seventh floor, then climbs the stairs the rest of the way. He does this every single day.

Yet whenever it rains, he rides the lift all the way up to the tenth floor. The lift works perfectly, and he is not doing it for exercise. Why does he stop at the seventh floor on dry days?
puzzle.approach: Ask what changes on rainy days — the weather alters what the man carries, not how the lift works.
puzzle.answer:
The man is very short. He can reach the ground-floor button (so going down is never a problem) and the buttons up to the seventh floor — but not the tenth-floor button. So on ordinary days he rides to the seventh floor and walks up the last three flights.

On rainy days he carries an umbrella, and uses its tip to press the tenth-floor button — so he can ride all the way home.

word_puzzle.title: Tails You Win
word_puzzle.body:
Sort these 16 words into 4 groups of 4. Each group shares a hidden word that can be added to the END of all four.

GOLD · MAY · CAPRI · BLUE · SWORD · POP · GOOSE · DRAGON · PEPPER · CAT · STRAW · HORSE · UNI · JELLY · RASP · BUTTER

(Careful: a few words look like they could fit more than one group.)
word_puzzle.approach: Each group shares a hidden word that can be added to the END of all four members. Find the four endings, then sort the sixteen words.
word_puzzle.answer:
…FLY: BUTTER, DRAGON, MAY, HORSE (butterfly, dragonfly, mayfly, horsefly)
…FISH: SWORD, JELLY, CAT, GOLD (swordfish, jellyfish, catfish, goldfish)
…BERRY: STRAW, RASP, BLUE, GOOSE (strawberry, raspberry, blueberry, gooseberry)
…CORN: POP, PEPPER, UNI, CAPRI (popcorn, peppercorn, unicorn, Capricorn)

Traps: BUTTER, BLUE and GOOSE also make fish (butterfish, bluefish, goosefish) — but the FISH group is exactly SWORD, JELLY, CAT and GOLD, which forces the rest into place.
